- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Puerto Rico has a unique blend of Spanish, African, and indigenous Taino influences.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Christmas in Puerto Rico starts in early December and lasts until mid-January.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] December 25th is Christmas Day, a national holiday in Puerto Rico.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Traditional Christmas dinner in Puerto Rico often features roasted pork (lechón asado), rice, beans, tembleque (coconut pudding), and arroz con dulce (sweet rice pudding).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Noche Buena (Christmas Eve) is celebrated on December 24th with a late dinner, gift exchanges, music, dancing, and fireworks.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] January 6th is Día de los Tres Reyes Magos (Three Kings' Day), where children leave their shoes outside for gifts.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Parrandas are informal sing-alongs featuring traditional Christmas carols known as aguinaldos.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Posadas is a nine-day celebration from December 16th to 24th reenacting Mary and Joseph's journey.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Nacimiento is a traditional Nativity scene common in Puerto Rican homes during Christmas.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The coquí is a symbol of good luck and prosperity in Puerto Rico.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Traditional Puerto Rican cuisine during Christmas includes arroz con gandules (rice with pigeon peas), coconut flan, coquito (a Christmas drink), and tembleque.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Traditional Puerto Rican music includes genres like plena, bombafunk, jíbaro, and aguinaldo.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Plena is a lively, percussion-based music style originating in Ponce, Puerto Rico.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Bombafunk is a fusion of African and Spanish rhythms.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Jíbaro music features romantic ballads and storytelling lyrics.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Aguinaldos are traditional Christmas carols sung during the holiday season.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Traditional dances include plena dance, bombafunk dance, jíbaro dance, and parranda dance.
